findings.diagnosis: The prompt lets high-contradiction cuts through: it underestimates positions where the remainder of the sentence will almost certainly overturn or complete the prefix (preverbal fragments, subordinating openings, subject-only prefixes, and tail fragments that need a qualifier). In practice, cuts with very high contra (≈0.9) systematically destroy set quality and must be treated as effectively unacceptable even if cohesion looks okay.
findings.evidence: Occurs in the majority of cases (≈9 of 13) across short and mid bins: policy kept cuts whose per-cut contra >0.85 and whose inclusion alone reduced H_set to near zero (contra_kill=true in many examples). The shared pattern is prefixes that lack their predicate/qualification or leave an essential modifier to follow.

edit.target: Contra is a graded probability and affects the number only through the product;
edit.text: Treat very high contra as effectively disqualifying: if the estimated contra for a candidate exceeds a high threshold (choose a conservative value, e.g. 0.6–0.8), consider the cut unsafe and assign it a very low final score regardless of cohesion. Below that threshold, continue to combine cohesion * (1 - contra) as the target. This prevents strong contradiction risk (prefixes that will almost certainly be reversed or rendered misleading) from being rescued by moderate cohesion estimates.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt's examples and tie-breaking bias can push cuts earlier, producing isolated verb/predicate fragments or split multiword name/number/title packages. In trying to avoid cutting inside very short packages the model has learned to move cutpoints left, which can create preverbal or standalone-predicate fragments that are unsafe.
findings.evidence: Observed across mid-length bins (noted in the last_revision post‑mortem and visible in multiple cases in ≤7–≤10 bins). Revision history blamed example replacements for shifting cuts earlier; several sentences then had isolated verb or numeric/title fragments and worse H_set outcomes.
